What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could potentially read portions of process memory.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Access of resource using incompatible type ('type confusion') in Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

According to the CVSS metrics, successful exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to some loss of confidentiality (C:L), and integrity (I:L) but lead to no loss of availability (A:N). What is the impact of this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could view some sensitive information (Confidentiality), make changes to disclosed information (Integrity), but cannot limit access to the resource (Availability).

There are multiple update packages available for some of the affected software. Do I need to install all the updates listed in the Security Updates table for the software?

Yes. Customers should apply all updates offered for the software installed on their systems. If multiple updates apply, they can be installed in any order.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: ASP.NET Core Tampering Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Inconsistent interpretation of http requests ('http request/response smuggling') in ASP.NET Core allows an unauthorized attacker to perform tampering over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could send specially crafted HTTP/1.1 requests through a reverse proxy to an affected server. Successful exploitation could desynchronize request handling between the proxy and the server, allowing the attacker to inject an unintended request. User interaction is not required.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Azure Storage Library Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper neutralization of special elements in output used by a downstream component ('injection') in Azure Storage Library allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker who can supply a blob tag condition to an application using the affected library could submit a specially crafted value. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to delete recovery snapshots or blobs beyond the operation authorized by the application. User interaction is not required.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker could add unauthorized deletion options to a permitted storage operation, allowing recovery snapshots or blobs to be deleted when the application did not intend to authorize that action.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

Yes, the Preview Pane is an attack vector.

Are the updates for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021 and 2024 currently available?

Yes. As of October 15, 2025, the security update for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021, 2024 and Microsoft Office 365 for Mac are available. Customers running Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021, 2024 and Microsoft Office 365 for Mac should ensure the update is installed to be protected from this vulnerability.

According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R). What interaction would the user have to do?

An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office Outlook Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Stack-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could send a specially crafted email message to a target user. Simply viewing the message in the Outlook Reading Pane could trigger the vulnerability, without the recipient opening the message or clicking anything in it. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code on the recipient's system. Network access is required; authentication and user interaction are not required.

Are the updates for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021 and 2024 currently available?

Yes. As of October 15, 2025, the security update for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021, 2024 and Microsoft Office 365 for Mac are available. Customers running Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021, 2024 and Microsoft Office 365 for Mac should ensure the update is installed to be protected from this vulnerability.

Yes, the Preview Pane is an attack vector.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is network (AV:N) and user interaction is required (UI:R). What is the target context of the remote code execution?

This attack requires a user to open a specially crafted file from the attacker to initiate remote code execution.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could host a malicious server and convince a user to connect to it from an affected client. When the client processes the server's response, the attacker could execute code on the client system. User interaction is required.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: SQL Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable October 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

Update Number Title Version Apply if current product version is… This security update also includes servicing releases up through…
5126967 SQL Server 2025 CU9+GDR (October GDR 2026) 17.0.5015.4 17.0.4006.2 - 17.0.5005.3 KB5122048 - SQL2025 RTM CU9
5128492 SQL Server 2025 RTM+GDR (October GDR 2026) 17.0.1145.4 17.0.1000.7 - 17.0.1135.8 KB5122770 - Previous SQL2025 RTM GDR
5126934 SQL Server 2022 CU27+GDR1 (October GDR 2026) 16.0.4305.5 16.0.4003.1 - 16.0.4295.3 KB5104824 - SQL2022 RTM CU27
5128493 SQL Server 2022 RTM+GDR (October GDR 2026) 16.0.1210.3 16.0.1000.6 - 16.0.1200.5 KB5122771 - Previous SQL2022 RTM GDR
5128494 SQL Server 2019 CU32+GDR (October GDR 2026) 15.0.4500.2 15.0.4003.23 - 15.0.4490.9 KB5122772 - Previous SQL2019 RTM CU32 GDR
5128495 SQL Server 2019 RTM+GDR (October GDR 2026) 15.0.2200.2 15.0.2000.5 - 15.0.2190.7 KB5122773 - Previous SQL2019 RTM GDR
5128496 SQL Server 2017 CU31+GDR (October GDR 2026) 14.0.3560.2 14.0.3006.16 - 14.0.3550.4 KB5122774 - Previous SQL2017 RTM CU31 GDR
5128497 SQL Server 2017 RTM+GDR (October GDR 2026) 14.0.2140.2 14.0.1000.169 - 14.0.2130.4 KB5122775 - Previous SQL2017 RTM GDR

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with low-level access to an affected server could send a specially crafted request to execute code on the server. User interaction is not required.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office SharePoint Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: No cwe for this issue in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

I am running SharePoint Server 2016. Do the updates for SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016 also apply to the version I am running?

Yes. The same KB number applies to both SharePoint Server 2016 and SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016. Customers running either version should install the security update to be protected from this vulnerability.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain ELEVATED privileges, which may allow them to perform actions beyond their original permissions.

How could an attacker exploit the vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with access to the domain could perform remote code execution on the SharePoint server to elevate themselves to SharePoint admin.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Use after free in Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability?

An attacker could use this vulnerability to elevate privileges from a Low Integrity Level in a contained ("sandboxed") execution environment to a Medium Integrity Level or a High Integrity Level.

Please refer to AppContainer isolation and Mandatory Integrity Control for more information.

According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R). What interaction would the user have to do?

The user must visit the attacker‑controlled webpage, and perform the two tap gestures that cause autofill to activate.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability?

According to the CVSS metrics, successful exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to major loss of confidentiality (C:H), but lead to no loss of integrity (I:N) or availability (A:N). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

This vulnerability could allow an attacker to disclose confidential information such as encrypted credentials but does not allow the attacker to modify any data or make the service unavailable.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Exchange Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Weak authentication in Microsoft Exchange Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Is Exchange Online affected, and do Exchange Online customers need to take action?

Microsoft has already deployed a related service-side fix to Exchange Online. Exchange Online customers do not need to take any action to receive the fix. Customers using affected on-premises Microsoft Exchange Server products should install the applicable security updates listed in the Security Updates table.

Where can I find more information?

Please see the Exchange blog for more information.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain unauthorized access to other users' mailboxes within the same organization and read email messages and attachments. The vulnerability does not allow access across tenant boundaries.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation More Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Raw Image Extension Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Integer overflow or wraparound in Windows Raw Image Extension allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by convincing a user to navigate to a folder containing a specially crafted RAW image file. The vulnerability can be triggered when Windows generates a thumbnail or preview; the user does not need to open the file. Successful exploitation could allow remote code execution.

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

The type of information that could be disclosed if an attacker successfully exploited this vulnerability includes unauthorized read-only access to the local file system.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Shell Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Windows Shell allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

What kind of security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could evade Mark of the Web (MOTW) defenses.

How could an attacker exploit the vulnerability?

In an email or instant message attack scenario, the attacker could send the targeted user a specially crafted file that is designed to exploit the vulnerability.

In any case an attacker would have no way to force a user to view attacker-controlled content. Instead, an attacker would have to convince a user to take action. For example, an attacker could entice a user to either click a link that directs the user to the attacker's site or send a malicious attachment.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: SQL Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Stack-based buffer overflow in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to have a deep understanding of the system and the ability to manipulate its components to trigger a specific condition. Successful exploitation is not guaranteed and depends on a combination of factors that may include the environment, system configuration, and the presence of additional security measures.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable October 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: .NET Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper verification of cryptographic signature in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could provide a specially crafted application that references an unsigned NuGet package. If a user restores or runs the application on an affected Linux system, signature verification might not be enforced, allowing untrusted package content to be installed or executed.

What kind of security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could bypass required NuGet package signature verification on affected Linux systems. This could allow an unsigned package to be accepted when signature validation is required by policy.

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Stack-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Word allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

Are the updates for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021 and 2024 currently available?

Yes. As of October 15, 2025, the security update for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021, 2024 and Microsoft Office 365 for Mac are available. Customers running Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021, 2024 and Microsoft Office 365 for Mac should ensure the update is installed to be protected from this vulnerability.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Revision.cvrf:Description: Microsoft is announcing the availability of the security updates for Microsoft Office for Mac. Customers running affected Mac software should install the update for their product to be protected from this vulnerability. Customers running other Microsoft Office software do not need to take any action. See the Release Notes for more information and download links.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office Word Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Word allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R). What interaction would the user have to do?

An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally. This means an attacker or victim needs to execute code from the local machine to exploit the vulnerability.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office Excel Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Excel allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

Are the updates for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021 and 2024 currently available?

Yes. As of October 15, 2025, the security update for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021, 2024 and Microsoft Office 365 for Mac are available. Customers running Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021, 2024 and Microsoft Office 365 for Mac should ensure the update is installed to be protected from this vulnerability.

According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R). What interaction would the user have to do?

An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office Click-To-Run Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Time-of-check time-of-use (toctou) race condition in Microsoft Office Click-To-Run allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). How could an attacker exploit this elevation of privilege vulnerability?

An attacker could exploit this elevation of privilege vulnerability by first establishing a foothold on the local system such as opening a malicious document or gaining access through another local vector and then leveraging the flaw to break out of the Protected View sandbox. Protected View is intended to isolate untrusted content in a restricted environment; however, successful exploitation would allow the attacker to escape these restrictions and execute code with elevated privileges on the host system.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office OneNote Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Microsoft Office OneNote allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted OneNote link and convince a user to open it. The link could cause OneNote to launch an attacker-controlled external target, which could lead to remote code execution; user interaction is required.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office SharePoint Tampering Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Observable discrepancy in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to perform tampering over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with access to an affected SharePoint form could submit specially crafted session data to the server. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to alter trusted application state and cause unauthorized backend actions; user interaction is not required.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to have a deep understanding of the system and the ability to manipulate its components to trigger a specific condition. Successful exploitation is not guaranteed and depends on a combination of factors that may include the environment, system configuration, and the presence of additional security measures.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office SharePoint Spoofing Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

How could an attacker exploit the vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability might be able to run their scripts in the security context of the current user by enticing the user to click on a link resulting in a cross-site scripting attack on the SharePoint Server.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Revision.cvrf:Description: The vulnerability associated with this CVE was fixed in July, however was inadvertently not included with that release. Microsoft recommends updating to the most current release of the SharePoint server.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: AAD App Proxy Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper authentication in AAD App Proxy allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Why are there no links to an update or instructions with steps that must be taken to protect from this vulnerability?

This vulnerability has already been fully mitigated by Microsoft. There is no action for users of this service to take. The purpose of this CVE is to provide further transparency.

Please see Toward greater transparency: Unveiling Cloud Service CVEs for more information.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Container Isolation FS Filter Driver (unionfs.sys) Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Concurrent execution using shared resource with improper synchronization ('race condition') in Windows Container Isolation FS Filter Driver (unionfs.sys) allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) Information Disclosure Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Observable discrepancy in Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

The vulnerable component uses a weak encryption algorithm or cipher. Traffic sent over a network by the vulnerable component could be decrypted and expose information related to a user or service's active session.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Remote Desktop Client Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Use after free in Remote Desktop Client allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires multiple conditions to be met. The attacker must have access to a user's machine and the user must have initiated an RDP session. The attack must also be carried out within a certain amount of time from the initiation of the RDP session.

GNU Aspell 0.60.8.2 (first vulnerable version is not known) contains a heap-based buffer overflow write (CWE-122) in its read-only dictionary loader. String::reserve() in common/string.hpp computes its capacity check with a signed int ((int)s + 1), so a requested size of 0x7FFFFFFF wraps negative and the backing buffer is never grown. ReadOnlyDict::load() in modules/speller/default/readonly_ws.cpp passes the unvalidated 32-bit size fields from a .rws dictionary header into this path, so a crafted .rws file with a valid endian marker (12345678) and an oversized length field (e.g. lang_name_size = 0x7FFFFFFF) causes attacker-controlled data to be written out of bounds past an undersized heap allocation. An attacker who induces a victim to load a malicious dictionary — for example via aspell dump master <file> — can corrupt heap memory, resulting in denial of service and potentially code execution. Fixed in b830b6e and will be fixed in release 0.60.8.3.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP Agent connection reuse can cause a client to accept as valid a response that was sent before the client has sent the request. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48931.
The guard that destroys idle keep-alive sockets when unexpected data arrives only runs when the event loop polls for I/O. If an unsolicited response has already reached the socket but has not been read yet when the socket is handed to a new request, for example because the event loop was busy with synchronous work, the guard is removed without seeing it and the data is parsed as the response to the new request.
This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

A flaw in Node.js DNS resolution allows hostnames containing a NUL byte to be silently truncated by the dns.resolve*() functions and dns.reverse(). This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48930, which only covered dns.lookup() and the net/tls host options.
Because the name is passed to c-ares as a C string, resolving attacker.example\0.trusted.example queries attacker.example and returns its records without any error. Applications that validate a hostname, for example against a domain allowlist, and then resolve it with dns.resolve*() can act on records for a different name than the one they validated.
This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification allows a certificate without a matching IP address SAN to authenticate a connection to an IPv4 address when the host is written with non-ASCII characters, such as fullwidth digits (`１２７.0.0.1`).
`tls.checkServerIdentity()` did not recognize such hosts as IP addresses, even though they normalize and resolve to a regular IPv4 address, and matched them against the certificate DNS names and Common Name instead. A certificate containing `DNS:127.0.0.1` or `DNS:*.0.0.1` could therefore be accepted for an IP endpoint it was not issued for. This is a regression introduced after the fix for CVE-2026-48618.
This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x** and **24.x**.

gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside the selected extraction directory. The write is limited by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not have this risk.

A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification can cause a server certificate to be validated against a different IP address than the one the client connected to, when the host is a non-canonical IPv4 literal with a leading zero, such as `0127.0.0.1`.
`tls.checkServerIdentity()` normalizes the host following the WHATWG URL rules, which read a leading-zero octet as octal (`0127.0.0.1` becomes `87.0.0.1`), while the connection is made through the operating system resolver, which on some platforms such as macOS reads it as decimal (`127.0.0.1`). A server at the connected address can then be authenticated with a certificate issued for another IP address.
This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

A flaw in Node.js Permission Model filesystem enforcement can grant access to paths that do not match a wildcard `--allow-fs-read` or `--allow-fs-write` rule.
When the requested path is shorter than the prefix of a wildcard grant, the radix tree lookup stops comparing early and treats the path as a match. For example, `--allow-fs-read=/etc/passwd.*` also allows reading `/etc/passwd`. This requires the wildcard grant to sit directly under the root of the permission tree, for example when it is the only grant for that scope. This is a different root cause from CVE-2026-58043.
This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**.

A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification allows a certificate with only a DNS SAN to authenticate an IP endpoint when the client connects using a non-canonical IPv4 spelling, such as `0177.0.0.1`, `0x7f.0.0.1`, `2130706433` or `127.1`.
`tls.checkServerIdentity()` did not classify these hosts as IP addresses, but normalized them to their canonical form and matched the result against the certificate DNS names. A certificate containing `DNS:127.0.0.1` and no `IP Address:127.0.0.1` SAN was therefore accepted, while the same certificate is correctly rejected for `127.0.0.1`. Exploitation requires a certificate with a numeric DNS SAN issued by a CA trusted by the client, and a platform resolver that accepts these spellings, such as glibc.
This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

A flaw in Node.js Permission Model filesystem enforcement leaves `fs.realpathSync()` without the required read permission checks. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-21715, which only covered `fs.realpathSync.native()`.
As a result, code running under `--permission` with restricted `--allow-fs-read` can still use `fs.realpathSync()` to check file existence, resolve symlink targets, and enumerate filesystem paths outside of permitted directories.
This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

A flaw in Node.js `crypto` causes the internal entropy caches used by `crypto.randomUUID()`, `crypto.randomUUIDv7()`, and `crypto.randomInt()` to be saved into user-land startup snapshots (`--build-snapshot`) and single executable applications built with `useSnapshot`.
If any of these functions, or an API that relies on them such as `URL.createObjectURL()`, is called while the snapshot is built, every process started from that snapshot returns the same values until the cache is refilled: up to 127 UUIDs and about 1,000 `randomInt()` values. Identifiers expected to be unique can collide across processes, and values issued by one process can be predicted by observing another.
This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

OpenPrinting CUPS through 2.4.20 contains a resource-exhaustion vulnerability in the submission-timeout handling of cupsdCheckJobs(). The scheduler suppresses timeout processing for all pending jobs whenever any client connection has an in-flight Send-Document operation, without matching that connection to the job being examined. A client allowed to reach the IPP service can hold an incomplete HTTP request containing parsed Send-Document headers before operation authorization, preventing unrelated incomplete jobs from expiring. Where Create-Job submission is allowed, incomplete jobs can accumulate until MaxJobs is exhausted and further legitimate print submissions are rejected. The suppression ends when the held connection closes.
vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: OpenPrinting CUPS before 2.4.20 contains a double-free in printer-class management. When CUPS-Add-Modify-Class replaces an existing class member list, add_class() frees pclass->printers without clearing the pointer. If subsequent validation fails, the class retains the dangling pointer; CUPS-Delete-Class subsequently frees the same allocation in cupsdDeletePrinter(). A client authorized to modify and delete classes can cause scheduler-wide denial of service. The default policy requires @SYSTEM privileges.

OpenPrinting CUPS before 2.4.20 contains a NULL pointer dereference in cupsdCheckJobs() when a job marked job-held-on-create refers to a temporary printer that has been automatically deleted. Temporary-printer cleanup can remove the destination without canceling its held jobs, and the scheduler dereferences the NULL result of cupsdFindDest() while checking holding_new_jobs. This terminates cupsd and interrupts all queues managed by that process. In some plausible scenarios, an unprivileged submission can trigger this.

OpenPrinting CUPS before 2.4.20 contains a NULL pointer dereference caused by repeated IPP group tags in job-creation requests. IPP parsing creates unnamed separator attributes with IPP_TAG_ZERO, but add_job() converts these separators to IPP_TAG_JOB. During job startup, get_options()/ipp_length() subsequently calls strlen() on a NULL attribute name, terminating cupsd and disrupting all queues. A single crafted Print-Job request can trigger the crash when the client can reach the scheduler and submit jobs to an accepting, enabled queue supporting the submitted document format. Anonymous submission is possible when permitted by listener and access-control configuration.
